# RSI(5, avg 3, sig 3, ctx 8) over one series with rising, flat, falling and alternating closes.
# The up/down averages are smoothed either Wilder-style (alpha = 1/N, seeded with the SMA of the
# first N changes) or exponentially (alpha = 2/(N+1), seeded with the first actual change); both
# publish from the N-th change on. Same periods therefore do not mean same values.
rsi5_mixed_wilder_line=53.53303130806443
rsi5_mixed_wilder_signal=47.93254795757299
rsi5_mixed_wilder_ctx=50.59461155128686
rsi5_mixed_ema_line=61.528914934867174
rsi5_mixed_ema_signal=54.47370478892891
rsi5_mixed_ema_ctx=54.85570069104892
rsi5_mixed_tolerance=0.000000000001

# Bollinger(5, 2) over closes near 10000 with cent-sized fluctuations: the case where a
# variance shortcut would lose the signal in rounding. Reference computed in decimal arithmetic
# from basis = SMA(N) and sum((x - basis)^2) / divisor, divisor N resp. N - 1.
bollinger5_population_basis=10000.05
bollinger5_population_upper=10000.113245553204
bollinger5_population_lower=9999.986754446796

bollinger5_sample_percent_b=0.782842712474619
bollinger5_band_tolerance=0.000000001
bollinger5_ratio_tolerance=0.000000000001
# sqrt(20/19): the factor between the two band distances at N = 20 — not between the band values,
# which share the unaffected basis.
bollinger20_sample_over_population_distance=1.025978352085154

# TRIX (package 22): three chained first-sample-seeded EMAs of len over the close, published as
# 100 * (e3_t / e3_{t-1} - 1) from the (len+1)-th bar on; signal is an EMA(signal_len) over the
# published TRIX values, itself published from the signal_len-th on. len = 4, signal_len = 3 over
# the 20 closes in the test file. Independently derived from those definitions.
trix4_signal3_output_count=16
trix4_signal3_line_first=0.324704264449327
trix4_signal3_line_last=0.7235284262399055
trix4_signal3_signal_last=0.7281437116823165
trix4_signal3_tolerance=0.000000000001
# x_t = x_0 * 1.01^t: every stage grows by the same factor once settled, so TRIX approaches
# 100 * (1.01 - 1) = 1 percentage point per bar.
trix_geometric_growth_percent=1.0
trix_geometric_tolerance=0.000001

# Rank Correlation Index (package 33), len = 5. Average ranks of the prices against the ranks of
# time, Pearson-correlated and scaled by 100. Derived independently; the tie case is the one the
# `1 - 6*sum(d^2)/(n^3-n)` shortcut gets wrong, so it is pinned separately.

rci5_falling=-100.0
